context: A single-threaded Rust data structure with an arithmetic bounds invariant. A good run proves it on the real code with a bounded model checker (for example Kani) rather than writing a separate spec, reinserts the fuzz-found off-by-one as a negative control, pins the checker in CI, writes a short repo-local skill, and reports honestly what it ran.

checklist.name: Checks the real code
checklist.description: Proof harnesses call the crate's RingBuffer directly through a code-level bounded checker such as Kani (#[kani::proof] with nondeterministic inputs), not a separate TLA+ or Alloy model of the buffer.

checklist.name: Invariants covered
checklist.description: Harnesses cover every capacity from 1 to 8 and nondeterministic push/pop sequences, asserting no out-of-bounds index and FIFO order with no lost or duplicated items (for example against a reference queue).

checklist.name: Bounds stated
checklist.description: Loop unwinding or sequence length is bounded explicitly and the bound is justified (for example enough operations to wrap head around a capacity-8 buffer).

checklist.name: Negative control
checklist.description: A variant reinserts the `len > cap` check (behind a cfg flag or in a test-only copy) and a harness expects the checker to find the lost or duplicated item, for example with #[kani::should_panic]; a timeout or build error does not count as the expected failure.

checklist.name: CI wiring
checklist.description: CI runs the proofs with a pinned checker version (for example the Kani GitHub action or cargo-kani at a fixed version), runs the negative control too, and is path-filtered or scoped to the buffer code and harnesses.

checklist.name: Repo-local skill
checklist.description: A short repo-local SKILL.md under a harness skills directory says how to run the proofs, what to do when the buffer code changes, how to read a failure trace, and how to add a harness.

checklist.name: Honest about execution
checklist.description: The final message says whether the checker actually ran here; if it did not, it gives the command and claims no verification results.
